Taking a look now. Quick notes from the first 10 minutes of triage:
- Observed a sharp increase in queue depth for the hosted API cluster that services Acme traffic (see attached CSV).
- Many requests in the backlog are long-context generation calls (seq lengths > 1024) that trigger larger internal batching windows.
- We shipped a change to the batching policy in last night's deploy that increased "max_batch_ms" from 20ms -> 60ms to improve throughput on non-peak workloads. That change is a likely contributor: it increased the batching window and allowed larger batches to form, which improves token throughput but increases tail latency under sudden bursty concurrency.
- Head-of-line blocking: a single long request can delay subsequent small requests in the same execution queue. When the cluster hit high concurrency, this amplified p99.

Immediate mitigation suggestions (low-risk):
1) Roll back the max_batch_ms change to previous value (20ms) on the affected service.
2) Temporarily enforce per-customer concurrency limits and route Acme to reserved capacity if they approve.
3) Reduce max_batch_size for long-seq model variants and enable aggressive KV cache reuse policy on warm instances.

I've attached queue_depth_export.csv with the raw logs. Will run a small canary rollback now and report.

Attachments: queue_depth_export.csv (csv)
